newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 25.

text.p: The Federal Reserve left short-term interest rates unchanged, leading bond prices higher while stock prices ended mixed, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
* AT&T Corp said its third-quarter profit would fall below analysts' expectations, triggering a 9.8-percent slide in its share price.

* The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission staff has notified two senior Merrill Lynch executives it is prepared to recommend charging them with civil securities law violations stemming from the 1994 collapse of the investment pool of Orange County, California.
* Loral Space & Communications Ltd is close to a deal to buy AT&T's broadcast satellite unit for more than $700 million.
* Consumer confidence in September remained near its highest level in since the early 1990's.
* Loewen Group Inc rejected a $2.8 billion takeover bid by Service Corp International.
* Multinational companies invested a record $315 billion outside their home countries last year, a 40-percent rise from 1994, according to a United Nations report.
* The American Civil Liberties Union challenged a new Georgia law that makes it illegal in some circumstances to communicate anonymously on the Internet and to use trademarks without permission.
* Coca-Cola CO is forming a joint venture with France's Group Danone to sell Minute Maid orange juice in Europe and Latin America.
* Kaufman & Broad Home Corp said its quarterly net income nearly doubled from a year earlier.
* General Electric Co's NBC television network won the ratings race in the first week of the new fall television season.
* Short interest on the Nasdaq stock market rose 7.8 percent in the four weeks ended September 13.
* CompUSA Inc insiders have sold 293,089 shares since August 19.

* Sure, the skyrocketing use of credit cards at places like grocery stores and gas stations may hold the threat of long-term financial disaster for banks and consumers alike. But meantime, these mileposts on the road to a cashless society are an unqualified bonanza for the business of credit-card processors, like First Data Corp. - Heard on the Street.
* The bond market got a moderate boost Tuesday when the Federal Reserve, through its policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee, decided to leave interest rates unchanged. - Credit Markets.
